sb_prompt: DISCUSS RECENT SOCIAL CHANGES.  HOW IS LIFE IN AMERICA DIFFERENT TODAY COMPARED TO LIVING TEN YEARS AGO?
turns: Yeah, so basically, it's a lot more about money and less about community, I guess. Like, when I was a kid, if the pipes froze in my mom's house in the winter, we just got together and fixed them. Now, everyone just calls a number and expects a stranger to show up. Sometimes that feels kinda nice because not everyone knows a plumber, but other times it feels really impersonal. You don't have the same connection with your neighbors anymore. Does that happen for you guys out on the farm?

Yeah, actually it's pretty different here too, but mostly because we're just trying to survive on our own. I know a neighbor who lost his whole herd last year to some disease, and he didn't even call anyone to help, he just tried to fix it himself for months. It's tough, but you don't feel that lonely when you're stuck in it like you do in town.
Oh wow, that's a real shame about the herd. I mean, I guess it takes a certain kind of grit to just keep going like that, even when you're so isolated it hurts.
Yeah, it's kinda lonely but you figure out ways to do things yourself, like fixing my own tractor now instead of waiting for someone who might not even show up.

Oh man, that's exactly what I'm talking about with the pipes. I got stuck on a call last week with a guy in the city who wouldn't even come out unless I paid him upfront, and I had to spend six hours sweating in my own house trying to unclog a main line myself. It's just... frustrating, you know? You know your neighbors would have been there in five minutes if they were out there, but everyone's so wrapped up in their own little bubble now.
Yeah, man, that sucks, I feel for you on that whole upfront payment thing, but hey, at least you got the job done in the end right?
Yeah, it was a nightmare, honestly, had to use a camera snake and some chemicals just to get the water moving again.

Yeah, it was a nightmare honestly, but hey, at least you got the water working again, which is more than I can say for my own stuff sometimes, I spent two days under the bed trying to fix the wiring last winter and finally just gave up and called an electrician because I was so tired of failing at it myself.
Yeah, I guess the silver lining is that I learned a little bit more about how houses work, but damn, I still hate feeling like I'm the only one who knows how to fix the damn thing.
Yeah, I guess knowing a little bit helps, but sometimes it just feels like you're fighting a losing battle against your own stuff.
Yeah, that's the thing, though, I guess I just hate feeling like I'm the only one who knows how to fix the damn thing.
Yeah, I guess that's the thing, it's almost like there's no one to ask, so you just have to figure it out yourself or give up and lose everything.
I mean, it's just weird because ten years ago, if I hadn't known how to fix it myself, I would have asked my dad, but now I don't have that option so I just feel kinda alone in knowing the answer.
Yeah, that's exactly why I keep trying to teach my kid, you know, before it's too late.

Yeah, teaching your kid is the only way to keep that chain from breaking, honestly. My own dad passed away just a few years ago and he didn't leave me any of his old journals or notes, so now I'm flying blind with every new job, which is scary when you're dealing with something as critical as a house. But at least it's not *completely* alone like you, right? You've got your whole family around the barn to lean on when things go south.
Yeah, well, it's different because we're family, so if the kid needs to learn, there's always someone there to yell at him until he gets it right, but I get it, losing that safety net sucks.
Yeah, but I guess having my mom there to yell at me when I messed up the soldering is better than having nobody to yell at all, even if she's gone now, it's just... quieter out here.
Yeah, well, she did yell a lot, but at least she was right there when I dropped a wrench on my toe last week.

Yeah, hearing about the wrench on your toe actually made me feel a little better, you know? Because even though I'm stuck flying blind now, at least I know I'm not gonna freeze my own family out in the cold like you did with your herd.
Yeah, well, my wife did yell at me for a week until I fixed the handle on the barn door, but hey, at least she was there to help me move the boards once I finally got the hole drilled right.

Yeah, but you know, at least you got the boards moved and the door fixed in time, whereas I'm still sweating in my own house trying to figure out why the water is gurgling like that. It's just... different. You got your wife and kid right there to help you push through the worst of it, and I'm just stuck waiting for someone to show up who might not even come. Does your wife actually know how to use a wrench, or is she just good at keeping you from quitting?
She knows a little, enough to tell me when I'm about to crack a bolt, but mostly she just keeps me from giving up.
That's a relief, honestly, just knowing she's there to tell me I'm not an idiot makes all the difference.
Yeah, mostly she just keeps me from giving up, but she did help me find the leak under the sink yesterday, so maybe she knows more than I give her credit for.
Yeah, that's the thing, she found the leak under the sink all by herself while I was messing up the handle, and honestly, that's probably why I'm still sweating over the gurgling water right now.

Yeah, but it's not just about her finding it, she actually gave me the wrench to finish the job and told me not to touch the pipe again, which honestly was the only reason I didn't blow the whole sink apart like you did.
Yeah, but it's kinda nice knowing she knows what she's talking about, even if she did tell me to stop touching the pipe before I ruined everything.
Yeah, well, I guess that's why I gotta keep telling her the difference between copper and PVC before she starts cutting the wrong stuff, otherwise we're both looking at a new sink and no water.

Yeah, that's scary, but at least you have someone there to stop you from turning the wrench before it snaps, whereas I'm just stuck here listening to that gurgling sound waiting for a number to actually pick up.
Yeah, but look, I appreciate the lesson on the wrench, I just hope you don't drown in that gurgling water before you figure it out.
Yeah, I hope you don't drown too, and honestly, maybe I should just call the city hall tomorrow instead of risking it myself.
Nah, don't call the city hall, you'll never get a hold of anyone, just keep digging and if you crack a pipe you'll flood your whole basement, so maybe check the sewer vent first.
Yeah, I guess I'll check the vent, but if it doesn't work I'm definitely calling a pro before I flood the whole basement.
Yeah, vent is probably it, but look, I gotta let you go, my kid's hungry and I haven't made dinner yet.
Vent is probably it, but if it doesn't work I'm definitely calling a pro before I flood the whole basement.
Yeah, if you check the vent and it doesn't work, you're gonna want to find a pro before you lose the whole house, so I'll let you get to it.
Vent is probably it, but if it doesn't work I'm definitely calling a pro before I flood the whole basement.
Yeah, I mean, you'll hear from me if the vent doesn't work, but for now, just go check it and I'll let you get to it.
Okay sounds good, thanks for the advice.
Nah, just go check the vent and if that doesn't work, you call a pro before you flood the whole basement.
